Turkish border guards shoot 50-year-old man in western Idlib

The Turkish-Syrian border in northwest Syria – North Press

IDLIB, Syria (North Press) – On Saturday afternoon, Turkish border guards shot at and wounded a 50-year-old man as he was entering his farmland located in western Idlib near the Turkish border in northwestern Syria.

A local source told North Press that Riyad al-Kanou, 52, was shot by Turkish border guards while checking his land, adjacent to the Turkish border near the town of Harem in western Idlib.

The source added that “al-Kanou was taken to Harim Hospital in critical condition.”

He stated that the Turkish observation tower opposite the town of Harem shot the man with several bullets, one of which hit his body, despite knowing that he was there to check his land.

Hundreds of farmers who own lands adjacent to the Turkish border have since refrained from checking their lands out of fear of being targeted by Turkish border guards, who continue to directly shoot civilians.

Reporting by Hani Salem
